title: dev mode: `os dev` accepts plain-HTTP OAuth for MCP on any host (loud warning); production keeps TLS-required with no switch — the need behind fork PR #19342
body:
Path: 接一个 Agent(社区版走 MCP) | 缺项——no checklist item asserts MCP OAuth from a non-loopback host in dev mode | P2

Filed by the director seat, summon #25 (`session_012GcsUbuqFGBibkEDMRC1eE`), under ruling batch #207 item 1 (fork-PR intake, maintainer 「fork PR 的处理同意你的意见。」) as the card behind fork PR #19342, whose need the maintainer read as, verbatim: 「我理解实际需求是开发人员在开发环境要想测试 mcp，遇到要求https」. ⛔ Not a claim; `domain:services` (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth`), `priority:p2`.

## The need

A developer runs `os dev` and connects an MCP client from another machine or container (a LAN IP, `host.docker.internal`, a container hostname). MCP OAuth refuses plain HTTP on any non-loopback host (`isOAuthEligibleBaseUrl`: TLS required, loopback exempt, fail-closed — OAuth 2.1 §1.5), so the developer cannot test the agent step of the road from anything but the same machine.

## The shape ruled (rewritten under the ruling addendum of 2026-09-21T04:15Z — maintainer 「要（开发模式）」 + 「19342 同意兼容」)

- **Transport rule at deployment level** (Keycloak `sslRequired=external` semantics): MCP OAuth is eligible over plain HTTP when the deployment's host is loopback **or a private / link-local address** (RFC 1918 `10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`; RFC 4193 `fc00::/7`; `169.254/16`, `fe80::/10`). A public host keeps TLS-required, fail-closed, exactly as today (`isOAuthEligibleBaseUrl`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts:418`).
- ⛔ No configuration key and ⛔ no environment variable can open plain HTTP on a public host; the contributor's `OS_ALLOW_INSECURE_OAUTH_HTTP` escape hatch is **not** adopted as written.
- One loud startup warning whenever OAuth is served over plain HTTP (「OAuth 未加密:仅限可信内网」). Development mode is subsumed (a dev bind on a LAN address is a private address) — ⛔ no separate dev-mode branch point.
- Reasoning of record: a deployment already serving login and session cookies over plain HTTP gains nothing from OAuth refusing plain HTTP; the refusal only removes MCP from that deployment.
- Two readings the dev takes first and records on the PR: (1) whether the mainstream MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code) complete OAuth against an `http://` server at all — if they refuse, say so on the card; (2) the hostname case — an intranet hostname (`crm.corp`) is not an IP literal: choose between resolving the host and judging the requester's peer address (Keycloak judges the requester) and pin the chosen reading; a plain-HTTP reverse proxy on a public address whose peer looks private is a known false-safe — document it, do not add a key.

## Adoption of PR #19342

Cherry-pick or re-implement the contributor's eligibility logic and tests onto the internal branch, re-shaped to the private-address rule; keep their refusal tests for the strict spellings as the production arm's pins; `Co-authored-by: jinyitao123` in the commit. When this lands, close #19342 with thanks and the landing link (the seat does it in the landing stroke).

## Acceptance

On a private-address host (`192.168.x.x`, `10.x.x.x`, a LAN bind under `os dev`): an MCP client completes OAuth over `http://` and the startup log carries the warning; on a public host the same request is refused with the existing prescription; loopback unchanged. All three pinned. A platform-checklist item under the road's agent step is authored with this card.
